mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Thunderstorms which have developed on a weak surface boundary this afternoon may pose an isolated threat for severe hail/gusts. However, watch issuance is unlikely at this time

details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorms which have developed on a weak surface boundary this afternoon may pose an isolated threat for severe hail/gusts. However, watch issuance is unlikely at this time

details.label: Discussion
details.text: 21Z surface observations and recent visible satellite imagery show a weak surface boundary draped from the NE Panhandle into parts of southwest/south-central NE. While large-scale ascent remains nebulous/weak across this region, modest low-level convergence along the boundary has been sufficient for widely spaced thunderstorm development as convective temperatures have been breached (surface temperatures in the mid 90s to low 100s). Modifying the 18Z LBF sounding for current surface observations suggest MLCIN has become minimal near this boundary, with ample MLCAPE to support robust updrafts. Furthermore, modest low-level winds veer to westerly and strengthen with height through mid-levels (reference recent KLNX VWP), which will support sufficient deep-layer shear for organized updrafts. Ongoing high-based convection may pose a threat for both isolated severe hail and gusty downdraft winds. Still, cooler surface temperatures to the east of the boundary in NE suggest the presence of stronger MLCIN with eastward extent, and it remains unclear whether additional thunderstorms will develop/move off the boundary given nebulous large-scale forcing. Therefore, expectations are for the overall severe threat to remain fairly isolated, and watch issuance appears unlikely at this time

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.00-1.75 IN

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Potential continues for isolated damaging wind gusts and marginally severe hail. Watch issuance is not anticipated

details.label: Summary
details.text: Potential continues for isolated damaging wind gusts and marginally severe hail. Watch issuance is not anticipated

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Widely scattered to scattered thunderstorms remain ongoing along and south of a differential heating boundary/remnant outflow from northeastern Tennessee into western/central North Carolina. Weak effective shear (20 kts or less per latest objective analysis) is largely limiting storm organization, but 2500-3000 J/kg MLCAPE, modestly steep low-level lapse rates, and around 1.75" PW continue to support water loaded downbursts capable of producing isolated damaging wind gusts. Isolated instances of marginally severe hail have also been reported with the most robust cores within a zone of marginally steeper mid-level lapse rates (near 7 C/km). This potential is expected to continue for at least another 1-2 hours; however, watch issuance remains unlikely owing to the weak effective shear and resultant pulse-severe storm mode

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...UP TO 60 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...UP TO 1.25 IN
